title: From Hourly to Annual: A Salary Calculator UK Approach for Australian Pay

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

If you're looking to understand your annual earnings from an hourly rate, a **salary calculator UK** approach works well when adapted for Australian conditions. The core formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission.

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year. This matches the Fair Work Commission's stated weekly rate of $1,004.90 multiplied by 52.

### Using a Salary Calculator UK Method in Australia

A **salary calculator UK** typically uses the same weekly × 52 approach. In Australia, you also need to consider the fortnightly pay cycle. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight before tax.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour) applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most Australian workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS) has specific pay rates that increased from 1 December 2026. Always check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) to find your correct minimum rate.

Award rates often include classification levels based on skill and responsibility. A **salary calculator UK** style tool can help you compare your hourly rate against award minimums, but you must use the correct classification.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. The casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using a salary calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter the base rate and add the loading separately using the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide.

Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your salary. For example, on a $52,245 annual salary, your employer would contribute an additional $6,269.40 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay but is an extra benefit.

### Tax and Medicare

For the 2026–27 financial year, Australian resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Medicare Levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Example: Full-Time Worker on National Minimum Wage

- Hourly rate: $26.44
- Hours per week: 38
- Annual gross: $52,245.44
- Fortnightly gross: $2,009.80
- Super (12% on top): $6,269.45 per year
- Estimated tax (2026–27): approximately $6,767 (excluding Medicare)
- Medicare (2%): $1,045
- Estimated annual take-home: $44,433

This is a simplified estimate. Actual pay may vary due to penalty rates, allowances, salary sacrifice, or unpaid overtime. Always refer to your award or agreement.

### Using the Timesheet for Accurate Calculations

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, including super and estimated tax. It's a practical way to apply the **salary calculator UK** method to your specific situation.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
